calls.body: The Wild are near the top of the league for shot volume, but the Mammoth are one of the best at keeping shots away. Hot take: the Mammoth shut it down.

calls.head: Depth vs. Star power
calls.body: The Mammoth roll four lines, but the Wild lean on their top six. Utah is the league’s best for depth, and Minnesota is near the bottom. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Mammoth.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Wild take down the Mammoth
paras: Liam O'Brien and Michael McCarron dropped the gloves midway through the first. Mikhail Sergachev and Matt Boldy squared off later in the period. For Sergachev, it was his first fight since February 2023. For Boldy, it was his first fight since November 2024. The Wild’s Jared Spurgeon left early in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as week to week with a lower-body injury. The first goal of the game would have been Minnesota’s, but it was taken off after a video review early in the period. They got it back late in the period, when Joel Eriksson Ek officially opened the scoring on the power play. Vincent Trocheck and Danila Yurov fought later in the period. Kirill Kaprizov stretched the lead to 2-0 on the power play just 48 seconds into the third, and that one stood up as the winner. Maxim Shabanov made it 3-0 midway through the period. With the goalie pulled and less than two minutes left, Logan Cooley got the Mammoth on the board.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves for the Wild, and Karel Vejmelka stopped 28 of 31 at the other end.

Clayton Keller took three penalties on his own. The Wild killed all four Mammoth power plays. The Wild moved to 9-3-2, still first in the Central, while the Mammoth fell to 8-5-0, second in the Central.
